newsitem.title: UK: Kenwood shareholders to demand emergency meeting.
newsitem.headline: Kenwood shareholders to demand emergency meeting.

text.p: Shareholders in Kenwood Appliances Plc, which makes food mixers and other appliances, said in a statement on Sunday they will call for an emergency general meeting of the company.
The statement said UKAV Continuation Fund Inc (UKAV) and Kalco Investment Ltd had been advised by Julian Treger and Brian Myerson, principals of Active Value Advisors Ltd (AVA).

"The resolution proposed to be put to the EGM will call upon the directors of Kenwood to hold discussions with interested parties with a view to soliciting an offer for the entire issued share capital of the company," the statement said.
The move comes after press reports at the end of September that two dissident shareholders planned to shake up the company, after Kenwood issued a profit warning earlier in the year.
Shares have recently been rising amid reports that Treger and Myerson were building up their stake in the company. A spokesman for AVA said UKAV now holds a nine percent stake in Kenwood.
AVA said it had called the EGM because the companies shares have performed badly, falling from a high of 380 pence in January 1994 to less than 200 pence prior to UKAV's investment in August 1996.
Shares reached a low of 185 pence on August 1, but since then have recovered to a high of 245 on October 21. They closed closed at 242 pence on Friday.
AVA also said Kenwood's management has failed convince the market that it has a clear strategy to restore the company's fortunes and the share price performance.
"Kenwood is a good brand name with significant sales and a strong market position and no one would doubt its performance were it part of a larger group," said Treger in a statement.
"Kenwood lacks highly rate management with marketing flair, it has inefficient production systems, faces high distribution and administrative costs and has a worsening balance sheet."
Kenwood now has 28 days to issue its position, and then a further 21 days in which to hold the EGM, AVA said.
No one at the company could be immediately contacted for comment.
